connector: No new chapters today. Look back at Chapters 11 to 15: the straw, the chase, Betsy, the mud flat, and the coach. In Chapter 12 the prince gave Jemmy away. In Chapter 15 Jemmy went back for him. Today you finish your opinion paragraph.

a.raw: betsy thought she heard a shout echo through the princes forest
a.fixed: Betsy thought she heard a shout echo through the prince’s forest.
a.why: Betsy starts the sentence and is a name, so it gets a capital B. The forest belongs to the prince, so prince’s needs an apostrophe. A period ends it.

b.raw: jemmy saw a smile on the princes face
b.fixed: Jemmy saw a smile on the prince’s face.
b.why: Jemmy starts the sentence and is a name, so it gets a capital J. The face belongs to the prince, so prince’s needs an apostrophe. A period ends it.

vcloze1.h1: The prince sticks to Jemmy like a little sea creature on a ship. Which bank word is that?
vcloze1.why: a barnacle sticks tight to rocks and ships.

vcloze2.h1: Jemmy knows danger is coming before he thinks about it. Which bank word means that?
vcloze2.why: instinct is acting without stopping to think.

vcloze3.h1: The boys hide beside a raised bank by the river. Which bank word means that?
vcloze3.why: an embankment is a raised bank beside a river.

vcloze4.h1: Jemmy has searched river mud for years. Which bank word means that?
vcloze4.why: mudlarking means searching river mud for things to sell.

match.barnacle: A barnacle sticks to things. Look for the meaning about a sea creature.
match.instinct: Instinct happens without thinking. Look for that meaning.
match.embankment: An embankment is beside a river. Look for the meaning about a raised wall of earth.
match.mudlarking: Mudlarking happens in the mud. Look for the meaning about searching river mud.

items.title: Which is right?
items.q: Which sentence uses the right preposition?
opts: The prince stood in the middle of the road.
The prince stood at the middle on the road.
The prince stood under the middle of the road.
items.why: In the middle of the road: that is where the prince stood.

miss.1: Read it out loud. At the middle on the road sounds wrong.
miss.2: Under the road? He would be in the dirt!

items.title: Find the preposition
items.q: Which word is the preposition? Captain Nips cracked his whip in the air.
items.why: In sits in front of the air and tells where.

miss.0: Cracked is what he did. Look for the small word in front of the air.
miss.2: Whip is a noun. Look for the small word in front of the air.

items.title: Where, when, or how?
items.q: The coach stopped with a jolt. What does with a jolt tell you?
items.why: With a jolt is the way it stopped. It tells how.

miss.0: A jolt is not a place. It is the way the coach stopped.
miss.1: A jolt is not a time. It is the way the coach stopped.

items.title: Where, when, or how?
items.q: The coach stopped after a few minutes. What does it tell you?
items.why: A few minutes is time. It tells when.

miss.0: Minutes are not a place. They are time.
miss.2: It is not the way it stopped. Minutes are time.

items.title: The root spect
items.q: spectacle, prospector, spectacular. What do all three have to do with?
items.why: They all have spect, and spect means look.

miss.1: Carrying is the root port, from last week. These words have spect.
miss.2: Find the part all three share. What does it mean?

items.title: Count the beats
items.why: wa · ter · mel · on: four beats.

miss.0: Clap again: wa, ter, mel, on.
miss.2: Clap again: wa, ter, mel, on.

items.title: Soft or hard?
items.q: Say cabbage. Listen to the first letter. Is the c soft or hard?
items.why: The next letter is a, so the c stays hard.

miss.0: Look at the letter after the c. It is a, not e, i, or y.

money that kidnappers ask for before they let someone go
a small word in front of a noun that tells where, when, or how, like under, after, or with
the main part of a word. Other parts are added to the front or the end.
one beat in a word. Im-por-tant has three.
the last sentence of a paragraph. It says your big idea in a new way.
the opinion your paragraph sets out to prove

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. No new chapters today. Instead, think back over Chapters 11 to 15. In Chapter 12, the prince gave Jemmy away. In Chapter 15, Jemmy went back for him. What changed in between? That’s what we’ll look for today.
transcripts.guide1: Word study review. You’ll roll words with the root that means look, fix prepositions that are doing the wrong job, and roll long words to split into beats.
transcripts.guide2: No new chapters today. Flip back through Chapters 11 to 15 and find the moment you think changed the story most. Then do the Read Like a Writer box.
transcripts.guide3: Today you finish. Check that your paragraph has all five parts: a claim, a reason, an example with a chapter, the other side, and a conclusion. Then say what you are proud of.

notes.wordParts: The root spect means “look.” inspect = look closely into, spectator = one who looks on, respect = look again with care, inspector = one whose job is to look.
notes.grammar: A preposition sits in front of a noun and ties it to the sentence. It can tell where (under the straw), when (after the storm), or how (with great care).
notes.spelling: To read a long word, find the vowels, split between them, read each beat, then push the beats together: im·por·tant.
notes.wgrd: Good readers look back and find the moment that changed the story the most.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Did they show courage?

items.t: Jemmy runs from Cutwater and hides inside a hollow tree.
items.why: He keeps his head and finds a hiding place, even with an outlaw right behind him.

items.t: Cutwater asks where the prince is, and the prince points to the straw.
items.why: He gives Jemmy away to save himself.

items.t: Jemmy has the coach stop for the prince, even after the prince gave him away.
items.why: Going back for someone who hurt you takes courage.
